# fivenines_ssl_status (Data Source)

Days until each uptime monitor's TLS certificate expires, read from its last probe. A snapshot of now — no time range applies.

Soonest expiry first. Monitors with no certificate data (tcp, icmp and dns monitors, or one never probed) are omitted rather than reported as 0 days, so a missing monitor never reads as an imminent expiry. A negative value means the certificate has already expired. Requires the uptime monitoring feature.

Metrics are read on every `terraform plan`, so the values below change between runs by design — treat them as ephemeral and keep windows relative (`timeadd(timestamp(), "-720h")`) rather than pinning absolute dates. Referencing them from a resource argument produces a permanent diff; the intended use is `output`, `locals` and `precondition` / `postcondition` checks.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Days until each monitored certificate expires, soonest first
data "fivenines_ssl_status" "certs" {
  monitors = [for m in fivenines_uptime_monitor.public : m.id]
}

output "expiring_certificates" {
  # Everything renewing in under three weeks, for a report or a notification
  value = [
    for cert in data.fivenines_ssl_status.certs.items : {
      monitor = cert.name
      expires = cert.formatted
    } if cert.value < 21
  ]
}

# Fail the run while a certificate is close to expiry. Monitors with no
# certificate data (tcp, icmp, dns, or never probed) are omitted rather than
# reported as 0 days, so `soonest_expiry_days` is null when nothing is known —
# and the check below then fails instead of passing on an absent value.
check "certificates_valid" {
  assert {
    condition     = coalesce(data.fivenines_ssl_status.certs.soonest_expiry_days, -1) > 14
    error_message = "A TLS certificate expires within 14 days: ${try(data.fivenines_ssl_status.certs.items[0].name, "unknown monitor")}."
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `monitors` (List of String) Uptime monitor UUIDs to read. Monitors your organization does not own are omitted. May not be empty: an empty selection reads back as "no certificate data", which is indistinguishable from a healthy fleet.

### Optional

- `aggregation` (String) How `collapse_scope` reduces: `min` (default, the next certificate to expire), `avg` or `max`.
- `collapse_scope` (Boolean) Reduce the per-monitor values to a single value using `aggregation`.

### Read-Only

- `items` (Attributes List) Days to expiry per monitor, soonest first. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items))
- `soonest_expiry_days` (Number) Days until the next certificate expires — the lowest value in `items`, negative once expired. Null when no requested monitor has certificate data, so an alert on it cannot silently read a missing certificate as a healthy one.

<a id="nestedatt--items"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items`

Read-Only:

- `formatted` (String) The value rendered for humans, with its unit (`99.98%`, `2h 15m`, `12 days`).
- `id` (String) UUID of the instance, uptime monitor or task the value belongs to. Null for organization-wide values and for collapsed results, which describe no single entity.
- `name` (String) Display name of what the value describes.
- `value` (Number) The numeric value.
